Announce every status change of a revealed row, not only its revelation: its idea occurring (not yet occurred to being studied), its moment passing (to window closed), its lock-out as a Path Not Taken, its claim by a rival (UNIQUE), and its dead end. Otherwise a row changes state silently, which breaks the brief that no revealed breakthrough is left stuck without an explanation.
additions.source: workshop report l.338 (Tamsin's brief), l.291 ('this moment passed'); §1.4 l.164 (revelation fanfare)

additions.text: A missing status: a rival theory that is Revealed but not owned when its decisive experiment reports against it, or a frontier row once its axis has refused it. It can still be researched for its consolation ('A dead-ended breakthrough yields its consolation and its report'), but W3 means the screen must not go on presenting it as an ordinary target. It needs a 'known dead end' badge or status, distinct from 'owned but dead-ended' (R72).
additions.source: §1.2 l.74; digest W3 ('every report is true'), §4 l.1127

additions.text: Open question: what status does a revealed row have when its strategic-resource prerequisite is lost mid-game, for example when a trade agreement ends ('losing access until they secure an alternative source')? Does a row under study stop taking Insight, and does a 'not yet occurred' row's window keep running? None of the four statuses expresses 'paused for want of a resource'.
additions.source: §1.2 l.128-134; §6 l.1504; workshop report l.499 (environmental prerequisites not modelled)

additions.text: A row from a later era than the civilisation's development costs ×4 for each era it is ahead, falling as development catches up. The screen could mark such a row 'ahead of its time', which explains its slow progress and its falling Endeavour price without exposing the hidden meter.
additions.source: workshop report l.20, l.450, l.490 ('Insight becomes progress at the price in force when it is spent')

additions.text: Credit PH04 Scientific Method with the change in revelation: before it, theoretical revelation is rare; after it, theoretical CORE and STANDARD breakthroughs reveal their applications as the norm. This is a milestone of the same kind as SO05's routing switch and the diffusion phases (R49, R130).

corrections.problem: R67 says that under §4 a Space-era row's window stays open for a civilisation funding its focus, 'so such a row must not show as closed'. That overstates W16. The hold applies only while the row's focus is the funded one, and only to STANDARD rows: UNCOMMON, RARE and UNIQUE keep their odds, and incidental research keeps the usual windows.
corrections.fix: A Space-era STANDARD row's window cannot close while its focus is the funded focus. While the focus is unfunded, the window runs and can close, and the row then shows as 'window closed' and does not reopen. UNCOMMON, RARE and UNIQUE Space-era rows keep their normal windows.
corrections.source: §4 l.1206 ('Incidental research keeps the usual windows ... UNCOMMON, RARE and UNIQUE alternatives keep their odds'); workshop report l.392

corrections.problem: R65 says a row under study 'is never lost'. That holds only for the workshop's occurrence model. A Competing Solutions alternative under study is still locked out if its primary is discovered first, and a UNIQUE under study is lost permanently when a rival discovers it first. The harness models neither, which is why the report says 'never lost'.
corrections.fix: Add these exceptions. A Revealed alternative under study becomes a Path Not Taken if its primary arrives first, unless an Endeavour is running on it. A Revealed UNIQUE under study becomes 'claimed by <civ>' if a rival discovers it first. Both are transitions out of status 2.
corrections.source: §1.2 l.58, l.84, l.87; §1.4 l.184; workshop report l.464, l.499 (lock-outs and the UNIQUE first-come rule not modelled)

corrections.problem: R95 says a glimpsed row appears as 'not yet occurred' or as 'window closed', and stays Endeavour-eligible 'if its prerequisites are discovered'. It leaves out the transition to 'being studied': a glimpsed idea keeps its chance of occurring every turn its window is open. And the condition is redundant: a glimpse can happen only to a discoverable row inside its window, so a glimpsed row's prerequisites are always discovered.
corrections.fix: A glimpsed row starts as 'not yet occurred'. It then either occurs and goes under study (status 2), or its window closes (status 4). It can also be completed by an Endeavour or arrive by diffusion. It is always Endeavour-eligible.
corrections.source: workshop report l.460 (glimpse each turn a discoverable idea fails to occur), l.466; §4 l.1123

corrections.problem: R131 says 'RARE and UNIQUE rows never diffuse'. That is the simulator's simplification (l.459), not the design. §1.2 gives RARE rows a moderate diffusion roll bonus after the Printing Press and a large one after the Internet, and gives UNCOMMON rows a large bonus after the press. Only UNIQUE rows are exempt.
corrections.fix: Only UNIQUE rows are exempt from diffusion. UNCOMMON rows (before the Internet) and RARE rows get a bonus rather than automatic arrival. Under the proposed translation, a bonus means the idea occurs to you, or returns if lost, with a head start from the larger bonuses (a proposal, not decided). The pre-press roll bonus also applies to every non-UNIQUE tier.

corrections.problem: R71 says a locked-out alternative 'stays visible as a faded entry'. That is true only if it had been Revealed. An alternative locked out while still Unknown must stay invisible; otherwise the screen shows a breakthrough that was never revealed.
corrections.fix: Only a Revealed alternative locked out before it is discovered becomes a faded Path Not Taken. An Unknown alternative that is locked out leaves no trace.
corrections.source: §1.4 l.184 ('When a Revealed alternative ... is locked out'), l.162

corrections.problem: R124, R10 and R14 list only MI06 and MI07 (FOSSIL_FUELS_ABSENT) and WA10 (GUNPOWDER_ABSENT) as removed. That is incomplete. FOSSIL_FUELS_ABSENT also removes CH09 Petrochemistry, and GUNPOWDER_ABSENT removes WA10 'and all gunpowder-dependent breakthroughs', for example WA22 Cannons, which requires WA10.
corrections.fix: Add CH09 to the fossil-fuel removals, and 'every row depending on WA10 (e.g. WA22)' to the gunpowder removals. The screen must show none of them, and nothing may imply their absence.

corrections.problem: R82's hidden-info list covers only token providers. But any 'or' option in a prerequisite, and any alternative in a focus's 'Available from' line, can name an Unknown breakthrough or one that does not exist in this world. Computing's line names MC14 (RARE, 'rare early access') and 'QM-E03 ... the elemental-world route'. MC09 has '(MI07 + CH09) or (CH04 + CH07)', and ES05 has '(MI07 or MC09)', where MI07 and CH09 are absent in fossil-fuel-absent worlds. R27 and R41 repeat QM-E03 as a Computing opener with no hiding rule.
corrections.fix: Render prerequisites and focus-opening conditions from the world-derived ruleset, so that options removed by a Truth or an axis are never listed. Show an option only if it is Revealed or Discovered. Never use the design text's world labels ('elemental-world route'). The same applies to the conditions of unopened foci (R38, R39).

corrections.problem: R55 rests on §1.2's threshold model ('Insight is tracked per Focus Area', the float storage). In the candidate model a focus has no Insight pool or threshold. Its Insight goes straight into the hidden meters of its rows under study, converted at the price in force when spent, and Insight it cannot use spills to other foci. 'Accumulated Insight' per focus is therefore only a historical tally, not progress toward anything.
corrections.fix: Any per-focus figure is labelled as Insight received or spent, a history, and never as a balance or progress toward a threshold. Note that Insight spent on a row ahead of its era buys less progress than its face value.
corrections.source: workshop report l.488-492 (l.490 'at the price in force when it is spent'); §1.2 l.14, l.43

corrections.problem: R62 treats §6's trigger ('at >80% Insight threshold') as directly usable. In the candidate model there is no focus threshold. The nearest equivalent, a row's meter past 80%, would leak the hidden meter for a revealed row, or hidden occurrence for an unrevealed one.
corrections.fix: Mark R62 as a threshold-model rule awaiting translation, not a requirement as stated. Any murmur must be defined without meter fractions or unrevealed occurrence (see the open question on murmurs).
corrections.source: §6 l.1497; workshop report l.464 (occurrence hidden), l.488 (hidden meter)

corrections.problem: R59 asks the screen to name price discounts: 'MC14 halved by an Antikythera or Clockwork row', 'QM-E23 halves the Plenum Drive's final research', G06's halvings and similar. Agreed decision 3 restates the multipliers below 1 (and Mycological Knowledge's) as head starts, and removes QM-E23's Plenum clause. R59 therefore conflicts with R60.
corrections.fix: Show the multipliers below 1 as head starts ('starts half-studied'), not as cost discounts. Drop QM-E23's Plenum clause. Keep only true multipliers (per-city, era price, the W18 row multipliers, prematurity) as parts of a displayed price.
corrections.source: workshop report l.167 and l.175 (decision 3 agreed), l.149 (stale clauses)

corrections.problem: R52 says that while an Endeavour runs 'the player cannot also select a focus'. That reads as a lock. Each turn the player chooses either an active focus or an Endeavour, and choosing a focus stops the Endeavour, whose progress then decays slowly.
corrections.fix: Selecting a focus during an Endeavour is allowed, but the control states that this abandons the Endeavour, its progress decaying slowly and resumable later (R109).

corrections.problem: R106 says the Endeavour's remaining turns 'can be exact'. The target (2× the price at commitment) is fixed, but Insight income follows the civilisation's science output and varies from turn to turn. A prototype can also halt mid-build.
corrections.fix: Show the progress percentage and the Insight total exactly, and the remaining turns as an estimate at current income.
corrections.source: §1.2 l.39 (Insight is science output); workshop report l.493; §4 l.1218

corrections.problem: R94 and R120 say a revealed RARE or UNIQUE comes 'only from theory, observation or the Determinist Institute', and R99's list of sources also leaves some out. They miss Endeavour spin-offs, which 'reveal or discover an unrelated qualifying breakthrough', and espionage, by which spies steal concepts (UNIQUE rows cannot be stolen).
corrections.fix: Add Endeavour spin-offs (any tier) and espionage (any tier but UNIQUE) to the sources of revelation in R94, R99 and R120.

corrections.problem: R57's hidden info says 'the roll-bonus part of a Necessity modifier is an odd and stays hidden'. Under the agreed translation of the threshold terms, Necessity's roll bonus becomes Insight alone, so there is no hidden roll part.

style.composition:
What the player sees (TechPickerScreen extends PickerScreen; all sizes are in Unciv virtual pixels. The stage is ExtendViewport(h, h) with h = settings.screenSize.virtualHeight (BaseScreen.kt:75-79). The default ScreenSize is Small, 900x600 (GameSettings.kt:34, 333-338). On a 16:9 window that is about 1067x600 virtual px.)

1. THERE IS NO TOP BAR. PickerPane is a single vertical SplitPane: scrollPane(topTable) above bottomTable (PickerPane.kt:41-47, 65). The split is at least 0.85 (PickerPane.kt:34, 71), and the bottom bar is at most 150 px tall (PickerPane.kt:35, 70). On Small that leaves about 510 px of tree and about 90 px of bottom bar. In the upstream screenshot extraImages/Screenshots/TechTree.png (1847x1013 physical, about 1.175 physical px per virtual px), the bar is about 122 virtual px tall.

2. TREE AREA (top 85%). The tree is one big Table (techTable) centred inside topTable on a solid navy #000033 background (TechPickerScreen.kt:63-68, 100-101).
   - It scrolls in both directions in an AutoScrollPane with overscroll off (TechPickerScreen.kt:86). Input is mouse wheel when hovered (AutoScrollPane.kt:54-74), or drag and fling. That pane is built with an empty ScrollPaneStyle (PickerPane.kt:45, AutoScrollPane.kt:45), so the tree has NO visible scrollbars.
   - Layout is a grid: columns = tech.column.columnNumber (left to right), rows = tech.row 1..N (top to bottom) (TechPickerScreen.kt:155-161, 197-223). G&K has 18 columns, 10 rows, 80 techs and 9 eras (Techs.json). Empty grid slots are empty cells.
   - Row 0 is the era header strip. Each era gets one header cell spanning its columns (colspan) (TechPickerScreen.kt:163-195).
   - Each tech cell pads its button 20 px left, 60 px right and 2 px top and bottom, plus 7 px extra on top for the first row (TechPickerScreen.kt:204-206). That gives an 80 px horizontal gutter between buttons, which carries the prerequisite lines, and 4 px between rows. The cell pitch is about 345 px per column and about 62 px per row (screenshot: 402 and 73 physical px), so the full G&K tree is about 6,200 x 650 px.
   - Every cell in the current era's columns is filled dark teal #072E2B, giving a vertical band behind the current era (TechPickerScreen.kt:208-209). All other cells show the navy behind them.
   - A 1 px vertical era divider (grey at 60% alpha) drops 1000 px from the bottom-left of each era header (TechPickerScreen.kt:261-269).
   - Prerequisite lines run from the right-middle of the prerequisite button to the left-middle of the dependent tech. The elbows sit halfway across the gutter (TechPickerScreen.kt:271-372).
   - When the queue holds more than one tech, numbered queue-order discs are drawn on the queued buttons (TechPickerScreen.kt:374-392).

3. BOTTOM BAR (bottom ~15%). Solid #000033 (TechPickerScreen.kt:102), with a 3 px blue divider handle above it. The bar is one row of three cells (PickerPane.kt:49-61):
   - Left: a "Close" text button, pad 10. It closes the screen; Esc/Back is bound to it (PickerScreen.kt:48-53).
   - Middle: the description, growing to fill. It is a wrapping white 18 px Label with 10 px padding in its own small scroll pane, which does have 10 px scrollbar knobs (PickerPane.kt:52-56). It shows the selected tech's description: lines like "Buildings enabled:", " • Stock Exchange (+3 Gold; …)", "Reveals Aluminum on the map", with inline stat glyphs (TechnologyDescriptions.kt:30-75). Clicking it or pressing F1 opens the Civilopedia entry (TechPickerScreen.kt:88-92).
   - Right: the action button, pad 10, right-aligned. It starts disabled and reads "Pick a tech" ("Pick a free tech" in free-tech mode) (TechPickerScreen.kt:104).

4. OPENING. The screen opens from the top-bar science stat, the world-screen tech button (F6), a notification or the next-turn action. It scrolls to centre on the current tech, or on the tech named by the notification. It also selects that tech, so its description shows, if the tech is researched or the queue holds 1 or fewer techs. With no current tech, it centres on the first researchable tech (TechPickerScreen.kt:107-122, 474-481).

5. SELECTION
   - Left-click a tech: shows its description. If it is not researched and the game state allows it, the queue is replaced by the full path of unresearched prerequisites ending at that tech. The action button becomes enabled with two centred lines: "Research [first tech in path]" and "(progress/total cost of path)", e.g. "Research Printing Press / (537/7845)" (TechPickerScreen.kt:394-472).
   - Right-click: appends the path to the existing queue (TechPickerScreen.kt:445-450).
   - Double-click: confirms and exits, playing the Paper sound (TechPickerScreen.kt:219).
   - Clicking an already-researched tech: the button reads "Pick a tech" and is disabled (TechPickerScreen.kt:420-425).
   - If a unique on the path makes it unavailable, the button shows that unique's text, disabled (TechPickerScreen.kt:432-443).
   - Every selection recolours all buttons and redraws the lines and order discs (TechPickerScreen.kt:226-253).
   - Tech buttons are plain Tables: no hover state, no tooltip, no click sound on a single click.
   - Confirming writes the queue and pops the screen (TechPickerScreen.kt:129-143).

style.typography:
Font: the platform's default font. Fonts.DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY is "" (Fonts.kt:42), which gives Java's default "Dialog" sans on desktop (DesktopFont.kt:56) and the default Typeface on Android (AndroidFont.kt:82). The upstream screenshot shows a DejaVu-Sans-like humanist sans. Glyphs are rasterised at ORIGINAL_FONT_SIZE = 100 px (Fonts.kt:41) and scaled down: by default 18/100 (NativeBitmapFontData.kt:74), and per label setFontScale(size/100) (Scene2dExtensions.kt:350-367, 392-398). There is one weight, regular; no bold or italic anywhere. Markup colours are enabled (Fonts.kt:55).

Sizes, as virtual px of font height:
- Default label size 18 (Constants.kt:136): era header names, the description text, text-button labels and the queue-order numbers (TechPickerScreen.kt:382).
- Heading size 24 (Constants.kt:137) is not used on this screen.
- Tech name and turns are 14 px (TechButton.kt:30, 36). The name is left-aligned, does not wrap and ellipsises at 140 px; the turns are right-aligned in a 40 px cell.
- The settings fontSizeMultiplier (default 1.0) scales the raster size (GameSettings.kt:155, 239-241).

Colours:
- The default label colour is white (BaseScreen.kt:200-203; Skin.json:297-302 defines 'color' but code overrides it to white).
- Researched tech names are #9A6210; past-era header labels are #782E10.
- Text buttons use white text, or dark-gray #404040 on hover (Skin.json:364-373).

Inline glyphs: Unicode stand-ins are replaced by atlas icons inside text. Examples: ⏳ for turns (EmojiIcons/Turn), ⍾ for science, ⚙ for production, ¤ for gold (Fonts.kt:139-150). The description text and turn counts therefore show small icons inline.
style.iconography:
All icons are flat silhouettes tinted at runtime and set inside 'portraits', which are layered circles:
- An outer circle of size + borderSize (2 px) as the ring.
- An inner circle of the full size.
- A glyph at 75% of the size.
Defaults are a white inner disc, a black ring and a white glyph (Portrait.kt:33-144). Circle art is OtherIcons/Circle.png or TechIcons/Circle.png (178x178, white). Each icon family has its own circle copy to avoid texture swaps (Portrait.kt:100-101, 179).

Tech portrait (46 px on the tree): TechIcons/<Tech>.png is a 100x100 white silhouette. The glyph and the ring are tinted with the tech's era iconRGB darkened by 0.6, i.e. multiplied by 0.4, over a white disc (Portrait.kt:174-181). A Renaissance tech looks like a deep purple glyph on a white coin.

Unlock icons (30 px):
- Units and buildings: black glyph, white disc, black ring (Portrait.kt:183-193).
- Uniques: CHARCOAL glyph, or UniqueIcons/Fallback, a black 8-point star, when there is no specific icon (Portrait.kt:199-201). These stars are the most common icon in the strips.
- Resources: inner disc in the resource-type colour (Portrait.kt:148-172).
- Improvements: inner disc in the colour of their top stat (Portrait.kt:211-243).
- Wonders already built by another civ: red ring (Portrait.kt:195-197).
- Stat-based items: stat icon in a circle with a thin charcoal ring (ImageGetter.kt:284).
- At most 5 icons per tech (TechButton.kt:118-120).

Shapes come from the Minimal skin nine-patches in android/Images.Skin/Skins/Minimal (Skin.atlas). All are white and tinted in code:
- roundedEdgeRectangle: 52x50, corner radius about 20, used for buttons.
- roundedEdgeRectangle-mid: 38x38, radius about 15, used for tech buttons.
- roundedEdgeRectangle-small: 24x24, radius about 10, used for the icon strip.
- rectangleWithOutline: 3x3, a 50%-grey 1 px ring around a white centre.
Skin paths with no image fall back to a stretched 1x1 whiteDot tinted, so they render as solid rectangles with no rounding and zero minimum size (ImageGetter.kt:242-252). This applies to TechPickerScreen/Background, TechPickerScreen/BottomTable and General/Border (docs/Modders/Creating-a-UI-skin.md:62, 129-130).

The world screen's queue-order disc and the close/round buttons use OtherIcons/Circle via surroundWithCircle (Scene2dExtensions.kt:139-148).
style.states:
Each button's state is shown only by the fill colour of the inner rounded shape (TechPickerScreen.kt:226-248). The grey #B3B3B3 border ring, the white portrait disc and the dark unlock strip (rgba(17,17,17,0.7)) are identical in every state. Because the strip is translucent black over the fill, it shows as a darker shade of the state colour. Precedence is evaluated top to bottom:

1. RESEARCHED: gold fill #FFD700, name in brown #9A6210, no turns shown. A researched Future Tech, which is repeatable, is #7F3200 instead, keeps its turns and has a white name.
2. CURRENT (first in the temporary queue; skipped in free-tech mode): steel blue #4893AF, white name, turns shown.
3. RESEARCHABLE (all prerequisites met): green #1CAA00, white name, turns shown. This outranks QUEUED, so a researchable tech later in the queue still shows green.
4. QUEUED (on the path but not yet researchable): teal #0E5C56, white name, turns shown. With a queue of 2 or more, each queued tech also gets a numbered disc (28 px base-blue at 75% alpha inside a 30 px white ring) at its left edge.
5. OTHER / not yet available: CHARCOAL #111111 (pure black in the older screenshot), white name, turns shown.

There is no separate 'unavailable/locked' visual. A tech blocked by an OnlyAvailable or Unavailable unique looks like a normal non-researchable tech; only the bottom-right action button shows the unique's text, disabled (TechPickerScreen.kt:432-443). There is no hover state, no 'selected' highlight ring, and no dimming. Selecting a tech changes only the colours and the queue numbers.

Lines carry state too (TechPickerScreen.kt:291-301):
- White 2 px into researched techs.
- Green 2 px from a researched prerequisite to an unresearched tech.
- Blue #4893AF into queued techs: 4 px where the prerequisite is still unresearched (the path still to travel), otherwise 2 px. Blue lines are drawn on top.
- White 2 px otherwise.

Era headers show era state:
- Past: amber #FFAF00 with a brown #782E10 label.
- Current: teal #0E5C56 with a white label, plus the #072E2B column band.
- Future: charcoal #111111 with a white label.
All headers have a 1 px white frame.

The action button reflects the selection:
- Disabled #252B3E 'Pick a tech' / 'Pick a free tech' initially, or when a researched tech is selected.
- Enabled #334D80 'Research [X]' with '(progress/cost)' on a second line (TechPickerScreen.kt:456-463).
- Free-tech mode: 'Pick [X] as free tech' (TechPickerScreen.kt:483-492).
- 'Unavailable', disabled, when the path is empty.
style.notes:
1. Reference image: extraImages/Screenshots/TechTree.png (1847x1013) is an upstream screenshot. Sampled pixels match the code: navy #000033, era band #072E2B, headers #FFAF00 / #0E5C56, buttons #1CAA00 / #FFD700 / #4893AF / #0E5C56, border #B2B2B2, era divider #4C4C61, Close fill #334C7F. It predates CHARCOAL: unavailable buttons, future-era headers and the strip overlay are pure black there, where the current code uses #111111. Treat the code values as authoritative. The tutorial crop android/assets/ExtraImages/Tutorials/Pick technology.png (528x105) also exists.

2. Units: every number above is in Unciv virtual px. Scale is screen height / virtualHeight (Small 600, Medium 700, Large 800, Huge 1000). The screenshot works out at about 1.175 physical px per virtual px. A browser mockup at 1:1 CSS px should look right at around 1000-1100 x 600-700 px, or be scaled up uniformly.

3. Skin system: colours can be overridden per skin through jsons/Skins/<skin>.json, via skinVariants keyed by path (TechPickerScreen/CurrentTechColor etc.; SkinStrings.kt:50-103). The base game ships no such json (android/assets/jsons/Skins does not exist), so the SkinConfig defaults and code defaults above apply. The skin is 'Minimal' (Constants.kt:125-126). The full list of skinnable keys for this screen is in docs/Modders/Creating-a-UI-skin.md:129-136, plus General/Border at line 62.

4. CSS translation hints:
   - Tech button: about 265x58 px, border-radius about 15 px, 1.5 px solid #B3B3B3 border, state-colour fill, padding 5 5 5 0.
   - Portrait: a 48 px circle with a 2 px ring in the era colour x0.4, a white face, and an era-tinted glyph of about 34 px.
   - Name row: 14 px, 140 px wide, ellipsis, plus a 40 px right-aligned turns cell with an hourglass.
   - Strip: 195x36 px, radius 10, rgba(17,17,17,.7), padding 2 0 2 10, five 32 px icons with 5 px gaps.
   - Gutters: 20 px left and 60 px right of each button; 4 px between rows.
   - Lines: 2 or 4 px with 6 px chamfered elbows at the gutter midpoint.
   - Era header: about 22 px tall with a 1 px white frame.
   - Buttons: min-height 50 px, radius about 20 px, padding 7 13 7 12, #334D80; hover #65DC72 with #404040 text; pressed #409955; disabled #252B3E.
   - Body font: 18 px sans, white, on #000033.

5. Behaviour gaps worth knowing for the redesign:
   - The tree has no scrollbars and no minimap; the player scrolls by drag or wheel.
   - Era divider lines are a fixed 1000 px long.
   - Buttons have no hover or tooltip.
   - Selection is shown only through recolouring and the bottom description and action button.
   - The bottom bar is capped at 150 px, so long descriptions scroll inside it.
   - Right-click queues extra techs, and double-click confirms.

6. Line citations for PickerScreen.kt, PickerPane.kt and SkinConfig.kt are to the files themselves; I read them concatenated and re-based the numbers. No files were edited.
